question: Can any of the four actors under test retrieve posts from a discovered public Facebook Group?

groups_tested.name: USA Medical Health Group MD and Medical Billing

verdict: Group discovery works, but Group-post collection is not supported by the tested actors.

required_capability_if_unsupported.capability_needed: A dedicated Facebook GROUP feed scraper.
required_capability_if_unsupported.why: The four actors under test cover keyword search (scrapesmith, parseforge), page-feed retrieval (thedoor) and post comments (apify). None of them takes a group URL and returns that group's post feed.

candidate_actor.status: NOT part of this test's actor set. Earlier work in ../facebook/facebook_actor_recommendation.json records a verified pass on group 290657479460430 (run lwd1sFYEcsEnAx10X, 10 posts with text/author/time/engagement). Adding it would require approval since it is outside the four actors named for this test.

required_capability_if_unsupported.access_note: Only PUBLIC groups are in scope. Private-group content would require an authenticated session, which is out of scope for public-content collection.

records.name: LowkeyKiwi1099
records.text:
Help please 🙏 
I filed a VA claim for my mental health condition and it got denied. The reason they gave was that there was "no qualifying in-service event" — no complaints, treatment, or diagnosis in my service records.

Here's the problem: that's flat-out wrong.

I requested my C&P exam DBQs, and when I read them, the C&P examiner had directly documented my in-service mental health treatment — a diagnosis and medications from during my service — right there in the exam. So the VA's own examiner found the exact evidence the rater claimed didn't exist. The denial contradicts their own paperwork.

I've got a current diagnosis confirmed, and now I've got proof the in-service treatment is documented. From what I understand, the piece I'm still missing is a nexus opinion tying the two together — so I've got an appointment lined up with a psych provider to get a nexus letter.

My questions for anyone who's been through this:

Have any of you dealt with a denial where the C&P examiner's own DBQ contradicted the rater's decision? How'd you attack it? HLR for the error, or Supplemental with a nexus letter?

Any recommendations on getting a strong nexus letter, or providers who know how to write them for the VA?

Anything you wish you'd known before you appealed?

Not looking for anyone to do it for me, just trying to learn from folks who've fought this fight. Appreciate any wisdom. 🇺🇸

I look forward to applying my knowledge in a practical environment while developing the skills needed for a successful career in medical billing.
